Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 19-year-old female with 3-day history of dysuria, mild suprapubic “crampy” discomfort, malodorous urine, and one episode of visible hematuria. No frequency, urgency, flank pain, fever, nausea/vomiting, or GI disturbance.  
- Most consistent with uncomplicated acute bacterial cystitis (simple UTI).  
- Alternative considerations (DDx):  
  • Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis (medium likelihood given new partner, no prior screen, but no discharge)  
  • Urolithiasis (low–medium likelihood; single hematuria episode but no colic or flank pain)  
- Management agreed: empirical antibiotics (Nitrofurantoin OR Trimethoprim) for 3 days; hydration advice; cranberry juice optional; avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve; safety-net advice to seek review if fever, back pain, worsening symptoms, or no improvement by week’s end.  
- Advised pregnancy testing if any concern.  
- No laboratory tests or STI screen ordered at this consultation.  

Management Plan
- Empirical antibiotic: Nitrofurantoin OR Trimethoprim, one tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact dose/route not documented).  
- Increase oral fluid intake.  
- Consider cranberry juice to help symptoms.  
- Abstain from sexual activity until symptom resolution; continue condom use thereafter.  
- Safety-net: return or call if symptoms persist >3 days, develop fever, flank/back pain, or feel unwell.  
- Pregnancy test advised if any concern about missed period or persistent symptoms.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Uncomplicated acute cystitis (bacterial UTI) – High likelihood: acute dysuria, suprapubic pain, hematuria, foul urine odor, female demographic, no systemic signs.  
- Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis – Moderate likelihood: new sexual partner, no prior screening; absence of discharge lowers probability.  
- Urolithiasis – Low-moderate likelihood: episode of hematuria; but lacks flank/colicky pain or typical risk factors.
